slot.brief: For a specified exothermic gas-phase equilibrium, predict direction of shift on temperature/pressure/catalyst/inert-gas addition at constant volume — pure concept, easy statements.

stem: For the exothermic equilibrium $\text{N}_2(g)+3\text{H}_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2\text{NH}_3(g)$, which set correctly predicts the shifts?
options: Heating shifts left; compression shifts right; a catalyst and an inert gas added at constant volume cause no shift.
Heating shifts right; compression shifts right; a catalyst and an inert gas added at constant volume cause no shift.
Heating shifts left; compression shifts left; a catalyst and an inert gas added at constant volume cause no shift.
Heating shifts left; compression shifts right; a catalyst and an inert gas added at constant volume both shift the equilibrium.

verdicts.working: Heating favors the endothermic reverse reaction, shifting left. Compression favors the side with fewer gas moles (2 vs. 4), shifting right. A catalyst and an inert gas added at constant volume do not shift equilibrium.

working:
Forward reaction is exothermic: heating favours the reverse reaction (left).\nCompression favours the side with fewer gas moles: $2<4$, so right.\nA catalyst does not change equilibrium; inert gas at constant volume does not change reactant partial pressures.

Independent check: Heating favors the endothermic reverse reaction, shifting left. Compression favors the side with fewer gas moles (2 vs. 4), shifting right. A catalyst and an inert gas added at constant volume do not shift equilibrium.
solution:
Heating favors the endothermic reverse reaction, shifting equilibrium left. Compression favors the side with fewer gas moles, so it shifts right ($2<4$).
A catalyst does not alter the equilibrium position, and adding an inert gas at constant volume leaves the reactant partial pressures unchanged; neither causes a shift.
